rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2 and 4 - the authors run their own SDrOP economic simulation (Fig. 2) and build and test a POWEIr controller prototype on a small SPDI system over seven days in Cambridge, MA. Q2: Section 4.2, Figs. 6-7 - the prototype predictive controller delivered 100% of irrigation demand with a 0.3 kWh battery buffer versus 1.8 kWh needed by the simulated single-section reference, and on high-demand days had 19-46% higher solar irrigation reliability; Fig. 2 reports the 18-74% cost and 31-66% reliability gains but only from an unvalidated design simulation. Q4: Section 4.2, Figs. 5-6, 8-9 - measured battery discharge energy (78-98% less than reference), solar power prediction error, battery charging rates and pump power per number of open sections, i.e. the solar-profile-matching mechanism through which the controller reduces storage needs and raises reliability. Q7: Section 4.2 and Discussion - the authors state the controller met demand despite prediction errors only because it had a (small) battery buffer to draw from, and that SPM benefits are greatest for farms with high pumping power and irrigation requirements; Level 1 requires the pressure sensor placed downstream of filters and one-time calibration. Q8: Discussion - small-scale system (0.25 ha, 2 sections), seven days only, no crops grown, SSO benchmark simulated rather than measured, unrealistically low pump efficiencies, agronomy/soil-moisture models not validated, economic results need validation under other conditions and full-scale LMIC farms.
rows.notes: The specific figures in the passage (18-74% lifetime cost saving, 31-66% reliability gain) come from the SDrOP life-cycle cost simulation of a hypothetical 2 ha Kenyan farm at three well depths compared to a Grundfos-sized system; this model run uses design data and is not compared against measurements in this study, so by itself it would not count as own evidence. Q2 is answered yes on the strength of the prototype experiment, which measured reliability and battery use on a real (scaled-down) SPDI system, though lifetime cost was not measured and the comparison benchmark was simulated. Q3 no: the simulation and prototype address different cases and the simulation is unvalidated; the prototype's benchmark is itself a simulation. Q9 no: the percentage ranges are spreads across well-depth scenarios or test days, not dispersion statistics or propagated uncertainty for the cost/reliability result; SDs are given only for pressures and pump power.

notes: Full text appears complete (main text, appendices, references). Supplementary information (SI S.1-S.4) referenced but not included.
